title: Safe Core: Players Who Fit Every Build
brief: Which players help in most categories without forcing a punt, so they suit the balanced build recommended for a 12-team auction? Tiers must be by price range, with a note on which stable categories each one provides.
summary: A balanced build skips the projected top 20 and fills the core with players ranked roughly 25 to 75. The safest of them get their value from points, rebounds and assists, because those categories repeat week to week. Build around Markkanen, Jalen Williams, Murphy and Kawhi in the 20 to 25 USD range. Then add 10 to 20 USD players with no weak category, such as Alexander-Walker, Anunoby, Paul George, Wagner, Fox and Rollins. Fill the end of the draft with 1 to 5 USD players who also have no weak category.

sections.heading: What a safe core means in our league

paragraphs.text: The balanced build skips the projected top 20 players. It puts the 11 core players between roughly rank 25 and rank 75. The ceiling is lower, but the build is much safer. In our 144-player draft, that means most of your 200 USD goes to players ranked around 25 to 75. You do not spend 60 or more USD on one star.

The safety comes from replacement. If your best player gets hurt, you can find another player around rank 30 on waivers much more easily than you can replace a top 5 player. With daily FAB waivers and 6 adds a week, a balanced team can patch an injury within days.

Every player in this article is tagged as fitting every build, with no weak category flagged. So none of them forces a punt. The real questions are what each one costs and which of his categories you can count on every week.

Points, rebounds and assists are high-volume stats. They are the most stable from game to game. In head-to-head, players whose strengths sit in those categories are more reliable. A steady points, rebounds and assists player is worth more than one whose value comes from steals, blocks and percentages, because his production repeats more reliably.

Players who combine categories that usually do not go together carry extra value. Examples are rebounds with assists, or assists with steals from a forward. In this pool, Jalen Williams gives big assists and steals for a forward. Franz Wagner gives points and assists as a forward. Podziemski and Hart give a guard's assists plus rebounds.

Some players have no weak category but get their value from steals, threes, blocks or FG%. That group includes Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, McDaniels, Okongwu and Paul George. They fit any build, but their weekly output swings more. Pair them with points and assists players. Do not stack them as your core.

sections.heading: How to spend by price range

paragraphs.text: Above 35 USD sit Gilgeous-Alexander, Maxey, Haliburton and Jamal Murray. All four fit any build, but they are projected top 20 players, so the balanced plan lets other managers pay for them. If one of them falls to the experts' price range late in the auction, he is still a sound buy. That range is about 34 to 38 USD for Murray, mid-to-high 30s for Haliburton and 40 to 45 USD for Maxey.

From 20 to 25 USD, buy your anchors: Markkanen, Jalen Williams, Murphy and Kawhi Leonard. Markkanen and Murphy bring points and threes. Jalen Williams brings assists. Kawhi brings points and steals, but only near 20 to 24 USD because of his knee. Stop at the top of each player's range. Experts call 29 USD too high for Williams, and above 25 USD Murphy is priced on a role that came with Murray out.

From 10 to 20 USD comes the middle of the core. Alexander-Walker, Irving, Herro and Bane give points, threes and FT%. Wagner and Fox give points or assists. Rollins gives assists and steals. Anunoby, Paul George and Okongwu give steals and threes. This is where the build gets most of its depth, because market costs here often sit below expert values.

From 5 to 12 USD, take upside pieces: Harper for assists, LaVine and Powell for points, McDaniels for defense and FG%, and Coward as a balanced wing. For the last bench spots, use 1 to 5 USD fillers such as Podziemski, Hart, Wiggins and Mikal Bridges. If one of them disappoints, you can replace him from waivers.

Prices for several core players are disputed. For Murphy, Yahoo says 30 USD and ESPN says 12 USD. Josh and our past auction point to the low 20s. For Paul George, most experts see 10 to 15 USD as good value, while Josh would go up to 20 USD. For Markkanen, the experts give a round 3 grade that fits a mid-20s bid, but one mock already reached 30 USD. For Kawhi, ESPN's 40 USD value goes against the expert cap of 24 USD. For Mikal Bridges, ESPN's 26 USD value goes against an expert value of about 2 USD. In each case, our plan follows the expert range and not the higher site value.

Our playoffs are weeks 19 to 21 and end 2027-03-28, so schedules matter for a core you plan to hold. Dallas (Irving), Memphis (Coward) and Phoenix (Miles Bridges) play 4-4-4. Haliburton plays only 3-4-3. Minnesota (McDaniels) has a two-game semifinal week. The Knicks (Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, Hart), Miami (Wiggins) and Houston (Sheppard) have weak schedules. Plan to trade Knicks and Miami players before the 2027-03-04 deadline.

In the first two to three weeks, check minutes and role first. Kawhi's and Irving's back-to-back games, Jalen Williams's hamstring, Wagner keeping the point guard role and Rollins keeping his starting job decide whether these players stay in your core. A balanced build can drop a player who misses these marks and replace him from waivers.
